Key takeaways

  • No like-for-like Gen-4 price on Higgsfield. That model is not in the Higgsfield catalog. Compare official Runway API rates with other platforms that publish a Gen-4 or Gen-4.5 row.
  • Cheapest catalog rates are not the same model. Higgsfield Wan 3.0 is $0.0167/s on Ultra (annual). Runway API Grok Imagine 1.5 Lite is $0.02/s at 480p. Gen-4 Turbo is $0.05/s.
  • Unlimited is not sold to new buyers. Legacy monthly Unlimited plans move to Max after November 30, 2026, per Runway’s help center.
  • Krea can undercut official Runway Gen-4.5 and Veo 3.1 in the catalog, as estimates. Gen-4 Turbo on the official API is a cheaper, different variant.
  • Affiliate links never change this price order.

What do Runway and Higgsfield plans cost, and what happened to Unlimited?

On Nov 17, 2026 PT, Runway’s public pricing page still listed Free, Standard, Pro, and Max for individuals. Free is $0 with 125 one-time credits. Standard is $15 a month, or $12 a month billed yearly, with 625 credits a month. Pro is $35 a month, or $28 a month billed yearly, with 2,250 credits. Max is $95 a month, or $76 a month billed yearly, with 9,500 credits and a one-month credit rollover. There is no plan named Unlimited for new buyers on that page. <a href="https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/52068047744019-Unlimited-plan-is-switching-to-Max" rel="nofollow noopener" target="_blank">Unlimited plan is switching to Max</a>, last fully read Nov 15, 2026 PT, says eligible legacy Unlimited plans stay unchanged through November 30, 2026, then monthly plans move to Max at $95 a month. Higgsfield’s catalog plans, checked the same day as the Runway cards, are Starter $19 a month for 270 credits, Plus $59 monthly or $33 a month billed annually for 1,200 credits, and Ultra $129 monthly or $50 a month billed annually for 3,000 credits. The longer official-plan walkthrough is in Runway pricing per second.

    Which option is best for each use?

    Higgsfield Ultra (annual) is best for the lowest catalog rate we track on Wan 3.0 and several other non-Runway models, if you use every paid credit. It is not for a Gen-4 or Gen-4.5 price we can show, because those Higgsfield rows do not exist in the catalog. Runway API is best for official Gen-4 Turbo or Gen-4.5 rates, and for Grok Imagine 1.5 Lite at 480p. It is not the cheapest catalog route for Veo 3.1 Lite, where Krea is lower. Krea Basic (yearly) is best for the lowest Gen-4.5 estimate we track, and for Veo 3.1 Lite. It is not a substitute for official Runway Gen-4 Turbo. No line is given for a Higgsfield Gen-4 rate.

    • Higgsfield Ultra (annual). Best for: the lowest catalog rate we track on Wan 3.0 and several other non-Runway models, if you use every paid credit. Not for: a Gen-4 or Gen-4.5 price we can show. Higgsfield’s pricing page.
    • Runway API. Best for: official Gen-4 Turbo or Gen-4.5 rates, and Grok Imagine 1.5 Lite at 480p. Not for: the lowest Veo 3.1 Lite catalog rate. Runway API pricing.
    • Krea Basic (yearly). Best for: the lowest Gen-4.5 estimate we track, and Veo 3.1 Lite. Not for: replacing official Runway Gen-4 Turbo, which is a cheaper, different variant. Krea’s pricing page.

    No line given for a Higgsfield Gen-4 rate, because that row is not in the catalog.

    How do we calculate this?

    Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page (https://vidfare.com/about/).
